sample_unit: cases (vignettes, emergency department cases, nurse line cases)

links.outcome: Triage disposition agreement with nurse line standards; direction of discordant errors (under-triage)
links.effect: Single-turn 52.9% and multi-turn 55.7% exact agreement vs nurse line standards; discordant cases were mostly under-triage (natural 70.8%, multi-turn 69.0%, both P<0.0001).
links.quote: Discordant case recommendations represented lower acuity against nurse triage (natural: 70.8% under-triage,  P < 0.0001; multi-turn: 69.0%,  P < 0.0001).

links.outcome: Whether multi-turn simulated nurse-style questioning improved triage-disposition agreement versus single-turn
links.effect: Multi-turn 55.7% vs single-turn 52.9% agreement against nurse line standards; clinician-adjudicated agreement 48.2% multi-turn vs 54.1% single-turn; no consistent improvement.
links.quote: These findings suggest conversational interaction does not ensure safe triage-disposition alignment.

unlisted_practices: Reporting ordinal distance from standard and error direction in triage evaluations of symptom-guidance AI

screen.reason: Empirical study comparing single-turn vs. multi-turn interaction prompting practices for LLM-based symptom guidance and triage disposition against nurse line standards.

primary.practice: multi-turn conversational questioning vs single-turn interaction
